channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: GTA VI makes $3.79 billion on day one, Rockstar says
item.description: Rockstar says Grand Theft Auto VI took $3.79 billion in first-day worldwide retail sales, and 32.5 million copies were pre-sold.

item.title: Sunrise on the Reaping heads for a $110 million opening, Deadline says
item.description: The Hunger Games prequel took $21 million in previews and is tracking toward about $110 million, which would be the series' fourth best start.

item.title: Anthropic shares give back most of their debut gains on day two
item.description: After closing its first day at $97.17, Anthropic stock fell about 13.5% midday on November 20 to just above $84, near its $83 IPO price.

item.title: Apple is said to be building an AI agent that can run your Mac
item.description: Bloomberg reports Apple is working on an agent that could control Mac apps, browse the web and write code, based on a job listing it later removed.

item.title: California's attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over chips and China
item.description: AG Rob Bonta served Nvidia with an investigative subpoena asking whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China.

item.title: EU Commission confirms a cyberattack that used an AI hacking tool
item.description: The European Commission says attackers disrupted its systems for over 10 days, and CERT-EU says they used an AI penetration-testing tool named ARTEX.

item.title: Twitch calls GTA VI its largest game launch ever
item.description: Twitch says GTA VI was its biggest game launch, with 3.3 million viewers at once, Bloomberg reports. StreamCharts counted nearly 8 million in all.

item.title: Meta's Muse AI reportedly mixed up users' private conversations
item.description: After reports it read Signal messages, TechCrunch reports Meta's Muse agent also showed employees other people's childcare messages and bank balances.

item.title: NGINX fixes ten flaws, including bugs that could let attackers run commands
item.description: Researchers disclosed ten NGINX flaws, five of them memory-corruption bugs dubbed nginx2root, and F5 has released fixes.

item.title: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
item.description: Intuit is selling email marketing service Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, CNBC reports.

item.title: Signal adds a setting to block AI assistants from reading chats
item.description: Signal restricts screenshots in its iOS app and adds a Block Siri AI setting that is on by default, with Android protections where possible.

item.title: Trump says US firms building AI data centers abroad could face taxes
item.description: President Trump said at a White House news conference that companies building AI facilities overseas could face substantial taxes or restrictions.

item.title: Valve drops Steam Machine waitlists, blaming memory and storage costs
item.description: Valve says it will stop running Steam Machine waitlists because it does not know how many it can make or what they will cost.

item.title: Google's Gemini can now use apps on your Mac to finish tasks
item.description: Gemini for Mac can now operate apps, files and websites in the background, with a live preview and per-app permissions.

item.title: Google picks Blue Origin to launch its AI server satellites in 2029
item.description: Google chose Blue Origin's New Glenn for a dedicated launch of TPU-equipped satellites for Project Suncatcher, targeting early 2029.

item.title: Over 500 Google workers ask for an AI-free Search option for schools
item.description: More than 500 Google employees urged bosses to let schools keep traditional Search without AI, Bloomberg reports, after big districts weighed leaving.

item.title: Yellowjackets begins its final season on Paramount+
item.description: The fourth and final 10-episode season of Yellowjackets premiered on November 20, with the finale set for January 22, 2027, Forbes reports.

item.title: Ubisoft is down 1,100 staff in six months as it launches an AI subsidiary
item.description: After cutting 166 more jobs in Montreal and Quebec City, Ubisoft is down about 1,100 staff in six months and has set up an AI unit called Motherbrain.

item.title: Hackers exploit a critical Cisco Expressway flaw rated 9.8
item.description: Security firm F6 reports attackers used a Cisco Expressway flaw that lets unauthenticated users run commands as root, after a public exploit appeared.

item.title: European streamer SkyShowtime will shut down at the end of 2027
item.description: SkyShowtime, a joint venture of Comcast's Sky and Paramount Skydance, will close at the end of 2027, with its CEO leaving, Deadline reports.

item.title: World of Warcraft: Forever reaches 15 million players
item.description: Blizzard's World of Warcraft: Forever has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years, its lead says, as it passes 15 million players.

item.title: Alibaba's AI cloud revenue jumps 53% as profit triples
item.description: Alibaba's AI cloud and computing revenue rose 53% and quarterly net profit roughly tripled, the WSJ and MarketWatch report.

item.title: Nvidia is said to be near a deal for diffusion AI startup Inception
item.description: The Information reports Nvidia is in advanced talks to buy Inception, maker of Mercury diffusion language models, for over $500 million plus earnouts.

item.title: A bill for a federal film and TV tax credit gains dozens of backers
item.description: Twelve more senators and over 70 House members signed on to a bill that would create a federal tax credit for film and TV production.

item.title: Rockstar says the PS5 Pro is not powerful enough for GTA VI at 60fps
item.description: GTA VI runs at 30 frames per second on consoles, and Rockstar says even the PS5 Pro cannot handle its simulation at 60.

item.title: Meta's Muse Charm AI device is said to cost $300 with free 5G
item.description: The Information reports Meta's portable Muse Charm will cost $300 and include up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G data.

item.title: Google opens its Genie 4 world model to developers through the Gemini API
item.description: Genie 4 is now in the Gemini API, creating interactive 720p worlds at 24 frames per second with native audio and keyboard controls.

item.title: Sony misses a Game Awards GOTY nomination for the first time in 12 years
item.description: None of Marvel's Wolverine, Saros or Marathon made The Game Awards' Game of the Year list, ending Sony's 12-year run of nominations.

item.title: Nvidia stops shipping H200 chips to China after a $115.8 billion quarter
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia plans no further licensed H200 shipments to China, after revenue more than doubled to $115.8 billion.

item.title: Moonshot AI reportedly scraps a $150 million Nvidia chip deal in Indonesia
item.description: China's Moonshot AI cancelled a $150 million deal to use Nvidia chips at an Indonesian data center, The Information reports.

item.title: Stallone biopic I Play Rocky goes nationwide with a $15 million to $20 million forecast
item.description: Amazon MGM's I Play Rocky expands this weekend after earning nearly $1 million on fewer than 30 screens, with strong reviews.

item.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. TV studios are being combined into one
item.description: Skydance plans to combine Paramount Television Studios and Warner Bros. Television Group into Warner Bros. Television Studios, Cynopsis reports.

item.title: Deltarune Chapter 6 is structurally complete as work begins on Chapter 7
item.description: Toby Fox says Deltarune Chapter 6 is now structurally complete and the team has begun on Chapter 7.

item.title: HBO renews The Gilded Age for a fifth season
item.description: HBO has renewed Julian Fellowes' period drama The Gilded Age for a fifth season, with its fourth season the show's most watched yet.

item.title: Samsung reshuffles its chip and mobile leaders
item.description: Samsung named new heads for its memory, System LSI and mobile businesses, with Won-Joon Choi taking over mobile from TM Roh.

item.title: Sky says Love Island will stay free as UK regulators review its ITV deal
item.description: Sky's deal to acquire ITV assets is under review by Ofcom and the CMA, and Sky says Love Island and Coronation Street will remain free-to-air.

item.title: Slay the Spire 2 nears 8 million copies sold, an analyst says
item.description: An analyst estimates Slay the Spire 2 has sold nearly 8 million copies and uses play data to argue its fans are unusually devoted.

item.title: Shift Up says Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is handmade after AI video backlash
item.description: After backlash over an AI-made music video, Shift Up's boss said Stellar Blade: Blood Rain is handmade, while noting its developers still use AI.

item.title: Ebenezer is forecast to drop to third in its second weekend
item.description: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer is forecast at $8 million to $13 million in weekend two, as the Hunger Games prequel arrives.

item.title: Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life moves from Netflix to Hulu and Disney+
item.description: The 2016 Gilmore Girls revival leaves Netflix and arrives on Hulu and Disney+ on December 25, Cynopsis reports.
